items.titleZh: 红牛车手担忧墨西哥起步，维斯塔潘调侃勒芒式起跑
items.summaryZh: 维斯塔潘表示自己在墨西哥城有争夺杆位的速度，但最后一圈在13号弯锁死，他认为部分原因是诺里斯在最后一段略微挡道；由于周五与劳森的事故被罚退，他最终将从第五位起步。

media.altZh: 红牛车手担忧墨西哥起步，维斯塔潘调侃勒芒式起跑 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Red Bull drivers fear Mexico start, Max Verstappen jokes: “A Le Mans start would be just as quick”
items.summaryEn: Verstappen said he had the pace to fight for pole in Mexico City, but his final run was ruined by a lock-up at Turn 13, which he attributed partly to Norris slightly getting in his way in the final sector; a grid penalty for his Friday incident with Lawson means he will start fifth.
detailZh: 红牛车手担忧墨西哥起步，维斯塔潘调侃：“勒芒式起跑也一样快”
墨西哥站到第一个弯的直道特别长，起步预计将十分关键。被问及现在是否对起步比近几周更有信心时，维斯塔潘给出了明确回答。
尽管维斯塔潘表示自己在墨西哥城有争夺杆位的速度，但最后一圈在13号弯锁死——据这位红牛车手所说，主要原因是诺里斯在最后一段略微挡了他的道。
按最终的排位赛成绩，这位荷兰车手通常能获得第二排的发车位，但由于周五与劳森的事故被罚退，他将从第五位起步。
这在墨西哥似乎尤其令人痛苦，因为过去在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道，第二排往往被证明是一个很好的发车位置。在通往第一个弯道的直道上，尾流效应很强，因此错过第二排显得更加不幸。
“但你事先无法知道这一点。也许明天我们会想，‘第五名其实也没那么糟’，”维斯塔潘在围场接受荷兰媒体采访时笑着说道。
比发车格罚退更大的问题是，红牛在整个2026赛季一直受困于起步问题，而通往1号弯的极长直道可能会让这个问题在墨西哥变得更加痛苦。
车队领队洛朗·梅基斯已经表示，红牛今年无法完全解决这个问题，因为需要更改硬件，包括离合器，而这些只能在2027年引入。
尽管如此，梅基斯表示希望红牛今年仍能用现有硬件取得进展，就像它相比墨尔本赛季揭幕战已经取得了显著进步一样。
然而，当Motorsport.com问维斯塔潘，他对起步是否比最近几周稍微更有信心时，他的回答简短而直接：
“不，并没有，说实话。”
这部分与墨西哥城的各节练习与排位有关，当时练习赛的起步也并不完全按计划进行。周五，这位四届世界冠军甚至在车队无线电中说：“我觉得我起步冲刺能更快。比如，我在维修区出口末端做起步，简直是灾难。”
“我又一次起步，又一次灾难。为什么我们不干脆改变点什么？或者我干脆来个勒芒式起步，你懂吗？我跑过去，推车，跳进去。然后直接起飞去比赛。”
当荷兰媒体环节提到这番话时，维斯塔潘笑了：“也许我们真该那么做。我觉得那也一样快！”
稍微严肃一点说，维斯塔潘解释说，他没什么办法防止起步问题重演。“有一些事情，但更多是跟（车队那边的）程序有关。但起步本身，我对此做不了什么。”
这与维斯塔潘和队友伊萨克·哈贾尔在奥斯汀的评论完全吻合，当时两位车手都表示，尽管他们在驾驶舱里正确执行了程序，结果仍然不理想。
哈贾尔希望起步能比最近几周顺利一些，但他也强调这将是一次未知的探索——尤其是在周末早些时候出现若干技术问题之后。
“我希望情况会更好，但这个周末我们非常努力。不幸的是，在第一节自由练习中，我们没能跑多少，也没有进行起步练习。今天上午我们做了几次不错的起步，感觉还可以，所以明天看看吧。我们会需要它的！”
detailEn: Red Bull drivers fear Mexico start, Max Verstappen jokes: “A Le Mans start would be just as quick”

With the particularly long run to the first corner, the start promises to be important in Mexico. Verstappen has a clear answer when asked whether he now has more confidence in it than in recent weeks

Although Max Verstappen said he had the pace to take pole position in Mexico City, his final run was ruined by a lock-up at Turn 13 – according to the Red Bull driver, mainly caused by Lando Norris getting slightly in his way in the final sector.

The eventual qualifying result would normally have earned the Dutchman a place on the second row of the grid, but the grid penalty after his incident with Liam Lawson on Friday means he will start fifth.

This seems particularly painful in Mexico, as the second row has often proved to be a good starting position at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in the past. The slipstream is strong on the run towards the first corner, making missing out on the second row seem even more unfortunate.
“But you can't know that beforehand. Maybe tomorrow we'll be thinking, ‘That fifth place wasn't so bad after all’”, Verstappen laughed during his Dutch media round in the paddock.

A bigger problem than the grid penalty is that Red Bull has been struggling with its starts throughout this 2026 season, and the extremely long run towards Turn 1 could make that an even more painful issue in Mexico.

Team principal Laurent Mekies has already indicated that Red Bull cannot fully resolve the problem this year, as hardware changes are needed, including to the clutch, and these can only be introduced in 2027.

Nevertheless, Mekies expressed hope that Red Bull can still make progress this year with the hardware it has, just as it has already made significant improvements compared with the season opener in Melbourne.
However, when Motorsport.com asks Verstappen whether he has slightly more confidence in the start than he did in recent weeks, his answer is short and to the point:
“No, not really, if I’m really honest.”

This is partly related to the free practice sessions in Mexico City, when the practice starts did not go entirely to plan either. On Friday, the four-time world champion even said over the team radio: “I think I could sprint faster off the line. Like, I do the start at the end of the pit lane, disaster.
"I do another start, another disaster. Why are we not just changing something? Or it is better that I do a Le Mans start, you know? I run, push the car and jump in. And then take off for the race.”
When that remark is brought up during the Dutch media session, Verstappen laughs: “Maybe we should really do that. I think it would be just as quick!”

On a slightly more serious note, Verstappen explains that there is not much he can do to prevent a repeat of the start problems. “There are a few things, but they're more to do with the procedures [on the team’s side]. But the start itself, there's not much that I can do about that.”

This ties in perfectly with the comments made by Verstappen and team-mate Isack Hadjar in Austin, where both drivers indicated that although they were following the procedures behind the wheel correctly, the results were still not as desired.

Hadjar hopes the start will go a little better than in recent weeks, but he also emphasises that it will be a step into the unknown – particularly after several technical problems earlier in the weekend.

“I hope it will be better, but we tried very hard this weekend. Unfortunately, in FP1, we didn't get much running and we got no practice starts. We had some decent ones this morning, with an okay feeling, so let's see tomorrow. We're going to need it!”
keyPointsZh: 墨西哥站到第一个弯的直道特别长，起步因此很关键
维斯塔潘被问及是否对起步比近几周更有信心时给出了明确回答
keyPointsEn: The particularly long run to the first corner makes the start important in Mexico.
Asked whether he now has more confidence in the start than in recent weeks, Verstappen gave a clear answer.

items.titleZh: F1墨西哥大奖赛试图防止去年第一圈混乱重演
items.summaryZh: F1墨西哥大奖赛裁判向所有车队和车手发布声明，试图避免去年比赛中第一圈发生的混乱。莱科宁、拉塞尔、阿隆索和汉密尔顿的费拉利在第一圈进入1号弯时四车并排，维斯塔潘和莱科宁切过了草地。
items.originalTitle: F1's attempt to prevent a repeat of Mexico Turn 1 antics
detailZh: 一级方程式墨西哥大奖赛的裁判向所有车队和车手发布了一份声明，试图避免去年比赛中首圈混乱的再次发生。
兰多·诺里斯、马克斯·维斯塔潘以及查尔斯·勒克莱尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿的费拉利车队在2025年的首圈进入1号弯时四车并行。维斯塔潘和勒克莱尔都切过了草地。
勒克莱尔最初领先得很轻松，但在4号弯的左弯中减速，让诺里斯超过了自己。
事实上，五分之一的赛车在1号弯切过了赛道——基米·安东内利、卡洛斯·塞恩斯和利亚姆·劳森也选择了草地路线。
这使乔治·拉塞尔在第一圈中排在最前面四名之后，对比赛结果感到非常愤怒，他说：“我简直无法理解三个人怎么能简单地切弯并保持他们的位置。他们犯了错误，刹车太晚，他们犯了错误。
“但然后他们可以简单地切弯并继续，而且他们的错误并没有受到惩罚。
“所以我一开始就非常生气，然后，当马克斯在4号弯出赛道，又回到赛道上，对我来说这是错误的时间和地点，但同样，这也应该受到惩罚。”
拉塞尔会很高兴地知道，裁判们已经主动发布了关于今年在墨西哥第一圈如何应用驾驶标准指南的澄清。
“在第一圈以及任何恢复（在安全车或红旗之后）后的第一圈，在1到3弯，以及4到6弯，所有车辆默认将被视为既进攻又防守，”他们写道。
“因此，根据现有指南，任何在这些区域离开赛道并保持与后方紧邻的车辆（由裁判决定）的位置可能被视为获得持久优势，除非这种位置是通过4弯[在车辆在1到3弯区域离开赛道的情况下]或通过12弯[在车辆在4到6弯区域离开赛道的情况下]放弃的。”
“这为周日比赛中车手必须让位的地点设定了非常明确的指南，并且关键在于‘为了保持与后方紧邻的车辆的位置’而切线。”
“这意味着你不仅会因为离开赛道超车而受到惩罚，而且如果你通过切角避免失去位置，也可能受到惩罚。”
detailEn: Formula 1’s Mexican Grand Prix stewards have issued a statement to all teams and drivers to try to avoid a repeat of the opening lap shenanigans of last year’s race.
Lando Norris, Max Verstappen and the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton went four-wide into Turn 1 on the first lap in 2025, with both Verstappen and Leclerc cutting across the grass.
Leclerc initially emerged comfortably in the lead but lifted off into the Turn 4 left-hander and allowed Norris ahead.
In fact, a fifth of the grid cut the track at Turn 1 - as Kimi Antonelli, Carlos Sainz and Liam Lawson also took the grass route.

This left George Russell, who had a front-row seat behind the top four on lap one, furious after the race as he said: “I just struggle to understand how three guys can just cut the corner and maintain their position. They got it wrong, they brake too late, they made a mistake.
“But then they can just cut the corner and continue, and there was no punishment for their mistake.

“So I was pretty pissed off with that to start with and then, when Max went off the track at Turn 4, came back on, and it was wrong place, wrong time for me but, again, that should’ve been penalised as well.”
Russell will be pleased to know the stewards have proactively issued clarification of how the driving standard guidelines will be applied on the first lap in Mexico this year.

“On lap one and the first lap after any resumption [after a safety car or red flag], in Turns 1 to 3, and Turns 4 to 6, all cars will, by default, be considered as both attacking and defending," they wrote.

“Thus, in line with existing guidelines, any car leaving the track in these areas and maintaining a position to a car or cars within close proximity behind (as determined by the stewards) may be considered as gaining a lasting advantage, unless such position is yielded by Turn 4 [in the case of a car leaving the track in the area of Turns 1 to 3], or by Turn 12 [in the case of a car leaving the track in the area of Turns 4 to 6.]”

That sets very clear guidelines for where drivers have to yield positions for Sunday’s race and it’s that cutting the track to “maintain a position to a car or cars within close proximity behind” that’s crucial.
It means you can be punished not only for overtaking another driver by going off track, but if you avoid losing a position by cutting the corner.
keyPointsZh: 今年裁判将明确如何在墨西哥大奖赛第一圈应用驾驶标准指南。
keyPointsEn: The stewards will provide clarification on how the driving standard guidelines will be applied on the first lap at the Mexican Grand Prix this year.

items.titleZh: 平川亮临危受命完成F1首秀排位
items.summaryZh: 平川亮在墨西哥站临时接替奥康驾驶哈斯赛车，尽管最后一轮排位受交通影响，仍以第19名完成F1首秀排位赛，未能进入Q2。
items.originalTitle: How Ocon's replacement's really faring on his shock F1 debut
items.summaryEn: Ryo Hirakawa was drafted in at short notice to replace Esteban Ocon at Haas in Mexico and qualified 19th on his F1 debut, missing Q2 after his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.
detailZh: 平川亮原本准备在墨西哥周六早上进行惯常的跑步，这时他接到电话，得知自己将获得那个“我一直准备着”的机会，参加自己F1首秀的排位赛。
尽管通知来得仓促，这位哈斯临时顶替埃斯特班·奥康的车手仍对未能以第19名进入Q2感到失望，因为他最后一轮排位赛受到交通影响。
这位32岁的丰田长期车手、勒芒24小时耐力赛冠军和两届世界耐力锦标赛冠军，得到通知的时间异常晚，他将在本周末剩余时间接管奥康的赛车。
平川亮并非冷车上阵，他此前在FP1出场，这是他自2024年末以来第九次参加F1各节练习与排位，过去两年他还在2023和2025款哈斯赛车上累计行驶了4541公里（2822英里）。但即便如此，他仍是直接进入深水区。
第三次练习赛不可避免地是一节压缩而高强度的环节，没有车手比他完成的圈数更多。工作很高效，与比赛工程师劳拉·穆勒之间的沟通清晰顺畅，他们挤进了一次迷你长距离模拟、起步练习、排位模拟，并多次抓住机会改进他进攻维修区车位的方式。其中还包括一次不换胎的进站练习，让他也打磨了释放流程。这意味着他进入排位赛时相对自信，尽管他清楚还有很多需要整理的地方。
两位哈斯车手在第一节排位赛都完成了三轮，平川在首圈比车队正式车手奥利·贝尔曼慢0.330秒——那是一次刻意干净利落的保底圈——第二圈则慢0.304秒，两人都取得了相似的进步。主要差距在包含体育场路段和最后一弯的第三计时段，正如平川所指出的，“一旦打滑，你就要付出代价”。
平川在最后一次尝试中未能提升，最终以0.875秒之差位列第19，而他的队友晋级第二节排位赛。然而，这并非因为他在环节末段榨取抓地力峰值方面缺乏优势。
他在第一和第三计时段提升了自己的个人最佳成绩，但在中间计时段有亚历克斯·阿尔本在他前方。阿尔本并没有直接阻挡他，但制造了代价高昂的空气动力学乱流，让平川感到失望。时间损失始于第二计时段开始处的4号至6号弯，他进入时落后阿尔本4.5秒，随后在连续弯中进一步恶化。
平川亮表示：“我在6号弯以及高速路段遇到了交通问题，因此损失了大量下压力。说实话，进入Q2本应是轻而易举的事，这对我来说很遗憾，但能来到这里仍然很好，所以我没什么可抱怨的。”
那么他的说法站得住脚吗？我们至少可以用第一和第三赛段作为他速度的确凿证据，因此这些数据成立——下方图表中的虚线差值线显示，差距中有多少来自中间赛段（从4号弯之前到12号弯之前）。
鉴于平川亮在第一轮和第二轮之间跟随了贝尔曼，可以合理推测，随着赛道条件改善和他对驾驶的进一步打磨，他在中间赛段可能像队友一样相比上一轮有所提升。
这使平川亮在假设的中间赛段比他在最后一圈做出的成绩快了0.537秒，这将使他升至第15位，排在阿尔派车手弗兰科·科拉平托之前，并淘汰卡洛斯·塞恩斯而非他自己——尽管优势仅为0.066秒。在这条“未曾存在”的圈中，他会比贝尔曼慢0.372秒，这也与前两轮的节奏差距相符。
这并不能确凿证明他本可以进入Q2，但至少证明他声称自己本可以晋级的说法是合理的。车队领队小松礼雄也得出了类似的结论。
“平川亮是在最后一刻被临时安排进赛车的，考虑到这一点，我认为他做得非常出色，”小松说道。“在第三节练习中，他的进步非常明显，而Q1从来都是一个非常棘手的阶段，轮胎处于极限边缘，但他保持冷静，设法发挥出了大部分性能。
“遗憾的是，他在最糟糕的位置——高速弯道——遇到了交通问题。我不知道他本能否进入Q2，但应该会很接近。那本应是对他今天出色努力的回报。”
对于平川亮来说，能够真正有机会进入Q2已经算是做得不错了，但正赛中还有更复杂的挑战在等着他。
当被 The Race 问及一个怎样的周日才算理想时，他回答得很简单：“好的起步，好的第一弯，有很多新东西，所以就是执行好并尽我所能。”
detailEn: Ryo Hirakawa was about to go for his usual run on Saturday morning in Mexico when he got the call telling him he would get the opportunity "I've always been ready for" to qualify for his Formula 1 debut.
Despite the short notice, Haas’s shock Esteban Ocon replacement was disappointed not to reach Q2 in 19th place given his final qualifying run was compromised by traffic.

The 32-year-old long-time Toyota driver, a Le Mans 24 Hours winner and two-time World Endurance champion, received unusually late notice that he would take over Ocon's car for the remainder of the weekend.

Hirakawa wasn't driving it cold having run in FP1, his ninth outing since late-2024 in F1 sessions, and having also logged a combined total of 4541km (2822 miles) in the 2023 and '25 Haas cars over the past two years. But even so he was in at the deep end.

FP3 was inevitably a compressed, intensive session in which no driver logged more laps than he did. The work was efficient, with clear communication to and from race engineer Laura Mueller as they crammed in a mini-long run, practice starts, qualifying simulations and took multiple opportunities to refine how he attacks the pit box. That included one practice pitstop without a tyre change that let him also hone the release. It meant he went into qualifying relatively confident, even if he recognised there was plenty he needed to tidy up.

Both Haas drivers completed three runs in Q1, with Hirakawa 0.330 seconds slower than team regular Ollie Bearman on the first lap - a deliberately neat and tidy banker effort - then 0.304s slower on the second as both made a similar step. The main deficit was in the final sector comprising the stadium section and last corner where, as Hirakawa pointed out, "as soon as you slide you [pay] the price]".

Hirakawa failed to improve on his final attempt and ended up 0.875s down in 19th while his team-mate advanced to Q2. However, that was not down to him not having the edge when it came to extracting the peak of grip at the end of the session.

He improved on his personal best time in sectors one and three, but had Alex Albon ahead in the middle sector. Albon wasn't directly impeding him, but he created costly aerodynamic turbulence and left Hirakawa disappointed. The time loss started with a little given away through Turn 4-6 at the start of the second sector, which he started 4.5s behind Albon, and got worse in the esses.

"I had traffic from Turn 6 and also [in the] high-speed sections, so I lost a lot of downforce," said Hirakawa. "It was, I would say, easy to [reach] Q2, which is a shame for me, but still it's nice to be here, so I can't complain much."

So does his claim stand up? We at least have sectors one and three to use as definitive proof of his pace so those stand - and the dotted delta line in the chart below shows just how much of the deficit came from that middle sector (from just before Turn 4, to just before Turn 12).

Given Hirakawa had followed Bearman between runs one and two, it's reasonable to assume he might have made the same step as his team-mate in the middle sector relative to his previous run as track conditions improved and he better honed his driving.

That gives Hirakawa a hypothetical middle sector 0.537s quicker than the one he did on the last lap, which would have put him up to 15th place, ahead of Alpine's Franco Colapinto and eliminating Carlos Sainz instead of him - albeit only by 0.066s. He would have been 0.372s slower than Bearman on this lap-that-never-was, which is also in line with the pace deficit on the first two runs.
It is not definitive proof that he would have reached Q2, but it at least proves that his claim he could have advanced is reasonable. Team principal Ayao Komatsu drew a similar conclusion.

"Ryo was drafted into the car last minute, and I think considering that, he’s done a really good job," said Komatsu. "In FP3, the progress he was making was very clear, and Q1 is always a very tricky session with the tire being on the edge, but he stayed calm and managed to extract most of the performance.

“It’s a shame that he had traffic in the worst possible place, in the high-speed corners. I don’t know if he could’ve made it to Q2, but it would’ve been close. That would’ve been his reward for his great effort today."
To have had a realistic chance of reaching Q2 represents a job well done for Hirakawa, but a more complicated challenge awaits in the race.
Asked by The Race what a good Sunday would look like, he kept it simple: "good start, good first corner, a lot of new things, so just execute and do my best.”
